A deferral is §8.1/§12.2's documented degrade-rather-than-block path (internal/ipc/client.go's Send spools and returns instead of waiting), so the event is durable and the daemon replays it — its client-spool watcher does so while the run is still going — and every one of the 2130 requests was found by its own identity (session and tool_use_id) in a client spool, the daemon's WAL or the store's tool_use index. note: hook_ack_rtt is REPORTED, never gated: it is the client-side ACK round trip of 64 in-process observe.tool deliveries, each with a fresh nonce and a real lease, timed through the same ipc.Client a hook uses. Design §7.5 sizes the ACK deadline from it as AckDeadlineMs = L0IngestMs + ceil(slack99), where slack99 = p99(hook_ack_rtt) - p99(B-B) over this same run. The timed samples are preceded by 2 DISCARDED warm-up requests on the same session: without them sample #0 paid a session-registry insertion and a WAL segment create on top of the round trip, and at 64 samples with nearest-rank percentiles p99 IS the maximum sample, so that one sample became the number the deadline was sized from. Its traffic IS real hot-path traffic, so all 66 requests do reach the daemon's l0_ingest and hook_controlled histograms — but this run reads both of those for the gated B-A and B-B rows BEFORE any of the tranche is sent, warm-ups included, so none of it is inside either gated population, and the B-B this row

is differenced against contains none of its own deliveries. They are reconciled rather than ignored: a second status read after the tranche counts every one of them, warm-ups included, into the delivery ledger, so a deferral of this tranche's own cannot pass unnoticed. The in-process traffic that does sit inside the gated populations is the warm-up's, disclosed with its own computed proportion. A p99 over 64 samples is still that set's own top sample, which is why §7.5 takes the maximum across three runs rather than trusting one
